text:
Zoe: Heads-up — us-west1-b preemptible GPU pool saw 4 interruptions in a 12m window. Inference tail latency spiked and a few long-running pods lost in-flight KV cache.

Zoe: Quick paste of the node events we saw:
```
NODE: gke-preempt-gpu-3    Reason: PreemptibleInstanceInterruption  Time: 2026-03-16T14:12:03Z
Pod eviction: job/inference-worker-7  message=evicted due to node shutdown
Scheduler backoff: Pending pods piled up -> 15% API 429s to republish keys
```

Evan: Oof. Were those pods in the best-effort Q or did they have PDBs?

Zoe: Best-effort, no PDB. They’re long-lived transformer workers reusing KV cache across requests (stateful-ish).

Matt: Two prongs: 1) short-term operational buffer (small ondemand pool tagged as cushion) 2) medium-term policy (taint/tolerate and CA config).

Ashley: Agreed. For strategy: create a tiny on-demand node-pool in us-west1-b to absorb churn for stateful jobs. Taint it NoSchedule so only tolerant pods land there. That keeps burst cost minimal. :+1:

Evan: We should also update cluster-autoscaler flags to avoid racing when spots drop. Suggested tweaks: `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`, `--scale-down-unready-time=5m`, and enable `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` for heterogeneous pools.

Matt: +1. Also add a dedicated nodeSelector label for long-running inference: `gpu.reserved=ondemand`. Then patch the Helm charts for those services to include tolerations. Minimal code change: 
```yaml
# deployment snippet
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      nodeSelector:
        gpu.reserved: "ondemand"
      tolerations:
      - key: "ondemand-buffer"
        operator: "Equal"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
```

Zoe: Cost impact estimate? If we keep 2 on-demand GPUs in the buffer for peak hours, rough monthly delta = ~ +$6k (us-west1 pricing). Worth it vs 2-3 hours of fallout for customers.

Ashley: We can autoscale the buffer but keep min=1-2. Also set a budget alert in Cloud Billing to watch incremental spend.

ops-bot: [alert] preemptible-interruptions spike detected in us-west1-b — 4 interrupts in 12m (severity: medium). Link: https://console.redwood/alerts/54321

Evan: Ops plan proposal (quick):
1) Create pool `ondemand-gpu-buffer-usw1b` min=2 max=4 taint `ondemand-buffer=true:NoSchedule` label `gpu-buffer=ondemand`.
2) Patch inference deployments to add toleration + nodeSelector for a subset of pods (stateful workers).
3) Adjust CA flags in staging and roll to prod after 24h soak.
4) Add PDBs for long-running pods to avoid correlated eviction.

Matt: Commands I’d run (gcloud):
```bash
gcloud container node-pools create ondemand-gpu-buffer-usw1b \
  --cluster=my-cluster --zone=us-west1-b --machine-type=n1-standard-16 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1 \
  --min-nodes=2 --max-nodes=4 \
  --node-taints=ondemand-buffer=true:NoSchedule \
  --labels=gpu-buffer=ondemand
```

Zoe: Nice. Can we make the rollout tomorrow 03:00 UTC? I’ll own the change and smoke tests.

Ashley: I’ll schedule the CA flag change (staging) and coordinate with billing to enable the budget alert. Also will add a Grafana dashboard tile: `preempt_rate`, `tail_p99_latency`, `ondemand_usage` for the region.

Evan: One more safety: add a k8s EvictionHandler that gracefully transfers KV cache pointers on SIGTERM where possible. It won’t save all cases but reduces cold starts.

Zoe: Agreed. I’ll open the small PRs: (1) infra: create pool, (2) infra: CA flag changes, (3) apps: tolerations/nodeSelector, (4) ops: add PDBs + evict handler hook.

Matt: Cool. If we see persistent high preempt rates we’ll consider moving some heavy-state shards entirely to on-demand. For now cushion + CA tuning seems enough.
